Theme Foundry

The interview turns references, assets, and a feeling into a build contract. The agent returns twice: once with the extracted visual grammar, then with the look running on Terminal Delight.

measured Terminal Delight already has the rendering target: palette, effects, and skin files; hot reload; a live picker; a headless resolver; and three built-in skins. This proposal adds the repeatable agent workflow around them.

ONE BRIEF → TWO REVIEWS → ONE BUNDLE

Read first

  1. 1

    The interview ends in a build contract

    Every answer lands in a field the agent can build from: palette roles, state colours, geometry, texture, typography, assets, motion, and acceptance screens.

  2. 2

    The first review is visual grammar

    The agent shows what it intends to take from the references and what it intends to ignore. You correct the reading before a TOML file exists.

  3. 3

    The second review is the running screen

    Mockups establish direction. A dense live session decides whether focus, attention, and text still work. The agent owns every revision between those two reviews.

  4. 4

    Skin ideas and product ideas split early

    Flat panels and signal colours fit the present theme system. Live connection routes and Blueprint Reveal need runtime state and get their own feature decision.

  5. 5

    The supplied warp is a capture confound

    The source product is treated as flat. Barrel distortion, soft focus, and chromatic fringe belong to the desktop theme that captured these frames.

Extraction

inferred These five traits recur across the supplied frames. They are the first review: keep, reject, or amend each one before the agent writes the look.

01 ─□─Architecture is visible

Thin routes and junctions explain relationships without turning the screen into a dashboard.

02 ▣State is spatial

Position, containment, and edge light carry state before labels do.

03 ◉Colour is a signal

Cyan, blue, pink, and amber identify roles. Most of the screen stays aubergine-grey.

04 ▤Artifacts have a place

Design documents, mockups, and comments occupy named regions in the work.

05 H↔AThe human is drawn in

Review and intervention are part of the system diagram, not an interruption outside it.

excluded from the grammar

Purple-and-cyan copying, universal glow, barrel warp, large decorative code, and diagram lines that cross terminal text at reading strength.

AGENTIC FOUNDRY

This is a diagrammatic reconstruction, not a proposed Terminal Delight screen. Its job is to make the extracted grammar arguable without importing the photographed warp.

System boundary

The interview allocates each request before work starts. This prevents a moodboard from smuggling a renderer project into a TOML task.

Interview

The agent asks only what the supplied material cannot answer. Each round produces an artifact the next round consumes.

round 0 · intake

What did you hand me?

  • Which files may ship, and which are reference-only?
  • Which visual effects came from the capture environment?
  • Which Terminal Delight screen must the look survive?
  • What must remain recognisably Terminal Delight?
Phosphor Blueprint: nine frames, eight unique; reference-only; treat the source as flat; preserve dense terminals and existing CRT control.
round 1 · intent

What should the screen feel like?

  • Name the physical or professional analogy.
  • Name the cheap imitation we must avoid.
  • What should be brightest?
  • What should disappear until needed?
Example: a calm technical instrument panel. Avoid generic neon developer-tool styling. Attention emits light; furniture stays dim.
round 2 · grammar

Which repeated moves are load-bearing?

  • Geometry: square, round, clipped, or mixed?
  • Boundary: line, space, double rule, or shadow?
  • Typography: operational text versus conceptual labels?
  • Material: flat, luminous, woven, clay, metal, glass?
Example: flat 1px geometry; small mono operations; tracked caps only for conceptual labels; no universal glow.
round 3 · semantics

What does each colour mean?

  • Keyboard focus
  • Working versus planning
  • Needs human
  • Warning and failure
  • Unknown or unmeasured
Example: cyan working; periwinkle planning; pink human; amber execution/warning; muted red failure; unknown remains visually distinct from idle.
round 4 · boundary

What is styling, and what behaves?

  • Can the current theme and skin files express it?
  • Does it need runtime agent or artifact data?
  • Does it change interaction?
  • Would it affect frame time on a twenty-pane screen?
Example: ghosted static art can be an asset study. Live routes and hold-to-reveal topology are product features.
round 5 · proof

What would make you reject it?

  • Which screen exposes the theme fastest?
  • What must remain readable at twenty-one panes?
  • What state may never be confused with another?
  • Which effects must work at zero as well as non-zero?
Example: reject if the focus ring and working state collapse to one colour, if routes compete with terminal text, or if overlays look borrowed from another app.

Operating depth

A · skin maker

Produces one skin.toml from references.

Fastest path. It cannot carry palette, effects, assets, or the reasoning that made the file.

recommended

B · look bundle

Produces the theme, skin, approved assets, provenance, resolved token matrix, screenshots, and the decision record.

More artifact structure. It gives the next agent enough context to revise the look without replaying the interview.

C · visual theme IDE

Adds human-facing controls for every token and asset.

A separate product. It duplicates the agent's editing job and expands the UI before the foundry has produced one accepted bundle.

Bundle

phosphor-blueprint/ ├─ brief.md ├─ provenance.json ├─ references/ │ ├─ contact-sheet.webp │ └─ extraction.md ├─ theme.toml ├─ skin.toml ├─ assets/ │ ├─ marks/ │ └─ projection/ ├─ renders/ │ ├─ scratch.png │ ├─ dense-21.png │ └─ narrow.png └─ evaluation.md

The bundle is the foundry's memory

The runtime still consumes ordinary Terminal Delight theme and skin files. The bundle keeps the source material, rights, decisions, and visual proof beside those files while the look is being made.

inferred Promotion should copy the accepted runtime files into app/themes/ and app/skins/. The working bundle should remain intact as the provenance and revision source.

Decisions

These are the first interview frontier. Comment directly on each item, save the page, then send the note map back.

1 · Is the look bundle the unit we keep?

The runtime files stay simple; the bundle carries the sources, rights, reasoning, renders, and evaluation that let an agent revise the look later.

Recommendation: yes. A pair of TOML files cannot explain which parts of a reference were deliberate.

2 · Are two human reviews enough?

Review the extracted grammar before generation, then review the running look after the agent has built and corrected it.

Recommendation: yes. Add a third stop only when the source material contains incompatible directions.

3 · Should runtime ideas leave the foundry?

Blueprint Reveal and live connector routes need data, painting, performance work, and interaction. The foundry can describe and mock them without pretending a skin file can ship them.

Recommendation: yes. Produce a separate feature brief when a runtime idea survives the live-look review.

4 · Is Phosphor Blueprint the tracer look?

It exercises all three current axes, the capture-confound rule, state semantics, an asset set, and the boundary between styling and runtime behavior.

Recommendation: yes. Stop the tracer at a flat, working theme-and-skin bundle; keep Blueprint Reveal out of its acceptance test.

5 · Must every source asset carry a rights state?

The agent needs to distinguish owned, licensed, generated, and reference-only material before anything can enter a distributable bundle.

Recommendation: yes. Unknown rights remain unknown and block promotion of that asset, not the rest of the look.

Terminal Delight · agentic theme foundry · combined design gate

Sources: nine user-supplied reference frames; the shipped chrome-skin brief and implementation; direct resolver read-back from the installed binary.

Limits: no unwarped originals were supplied; no runtime topology overlay was prototyped; this page proposes the interview and bundle contract only.

Build contract

What the interview must settle before generation

Identity

Name, one-sentence intent, physical analogy, explicit anti-reference, target Terminal Delight screen.

Sources

Every file, its rights state, whether it can ship, and any capture confounds. Duplicate and contradictory sources are recorded rather than silently dropped.

Visual grammar

Geometry, boundaries, emphasis, density, typography, material, motion, light discipline, and the hierarchy of what gets noticed first.

Semantics

Focus, selected, working, planning, needs-human, warning, failure, idle, and unknown. Each gets an intended visual distinction and a collision test.

Runtime allocation

Each desired effect maps to palette, effects, skin, static assets, or a separate product feature.

Proof

Exact screen matrix, rejection criteria, performance ceiling, and the live session used for the final eye test.

Reference extraction

Phosphor Blueprint · proposed first review

Take

The stage rail, the design artifact at the center, connection nodes, low-contrast operational state, and a visible human review step.

Translate

Terminal Delight keeps terminals as the sharpest objects. Diagram lines live behind or beside work; colour rises only on focus and state.

Refuse

The capture's barrel warp, blur, and chromatic fringe. Also refuse a literal purple/cyan recolour and decorative topology that does not correspond to anything the app knows.

Question for review

Should the stage rail represent a generic design process, the software-factory gates, or the current harness's own reported lifecycle? Recommendation: use reported lifecycle data when available and omit the rail when it is not.

inferred The owner should see one contact sheet first, then the live dense workspace. Requiring live review for every intermediate edit would turn the agent into a cursor operator.

Styling boundary

The decision that prevents scope drift

Theme

Palette roles, ANSI colours, font, scanlines, vignette, glow, bloom, tracking, flicker, jiggle, and bezel treatment.

Skin

Semantic chrome inks, geometry metrics, corners, boundaries, selection emphasis, dividers, caps, and surface shine.

Assets

Files the renderer already knows how to load, plus provenance and a fallback. A bundle does not create a rendering surface.

Product

Anything driven by live agent topology, artifacts, user gestures, or timed state transitions. It gets its own acceptance criterion and frame-time test.

Blueprint Reveal

A hold gesture dims operational content and raises a live system diagram. That needs a topology model, a compositor layer, input handling, accessibility behavior, and a performance budget. The foundry may preserve the idea and draw its mockup. A skin cannot implement it.

Capture confound

The source product is treated as flat

Recorded fact

The user states that barrel warp comes from the desktop theme used during capture. It is not part of the original product design.

Extraction rule

Use the frames for layout, hierarchy, colour roles, borders, typography, and collaboration patterns. Ignore outer curvature, uneven focus, and edge fringing.

Invalidation

If flat originals are later supplied and they show authored distortion inside the product UI, revise the extraction. Until then, no theme decision may cite the captured warp as evidence.

Bundle contract

One revision source around two runtime files

brief.md

The approved visual grammar, exclusions, semantic colour map, and acceptance screens.

provenance.json

One record per source and asset: path, checksum, owner, rights state, permitted use, and derived outputs. An absent rights answer remains absent.

theme.toml + skin.toml

The files Terminal Delight can consume. Promotion may embed them as built-ins after live approval.

references + extraction

The evidence and the agent's reading of it. Keeping them together lets a later agent distinguish an intentional decision from an accident in the current values.

renders + evaluation

The proof screens, the conditions under which they were captured, the owner's notes, and the defects corrected after looking.
